To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the probability of GDVDV occurrence in a population of working dogs in Texas is positively correlated with atmospheric pressure.
minimum and maximum daily atmospheric pressures on the day of the GDV event and maximum daily atmospheric pres-sure on the day before were positively associated with probability of GDV.
the occurrence of gastric dilation-volvulus in working dogs in Texas is associated with atmospheric pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a statistical model for the study of the occurrence of GDVs in a population of working dogs.
the development of a new method for investigating the association between the occurrence of GDVs in dogs and weather events.
the application of the time series model to the analysis of the meteorological factors of a life-threatening disease in dogs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association between weather and the occurrence of the disease is weak and the risk of GDV in the studied population of dogs is high.
the association between weather conditions and GDV is not yet proven.
the occurrence of GDVs is positively associated with the atmospheric pressure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the occurrence of gastric dilation-volvulus in our population of high-risk dogs was associated with the minimum and maximum daily atmospheric pressures on the day of the event and with the maximum daily atmospheric pressures the day before the event.
the occurrence of GDVS in a population of working dogs is associated with the atmospheric pressure.
the occurrence of GDVS in the population of high-risk dogs is associated with the atmospheric pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time series model can be used to investigate the association of meteorological events and occurrence of a condition in a population of animals.
a time series approach is a promising method for the study of the occurrence of GDVs in large populations of dogs.
the binary time series model can be applied to veterinary data to study rare disease occurrence in a population.
